requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints` has no implementation edges and no review roots. I found no structural obligation that would need one. Each clause states only what a provider request must look like.

- "every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint after the system prompt ... and another at the end of its last message". This fixes where the markers go in the request. A different implementation could build the request with any function, type or layering and still produce the same request, so the choice is discretionary.
- "Cache checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request". This is a property of the output. Any code that produces the same content satisfies it.
- OpenAI: "MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests", "replay prior conversation content in its original order" and "MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks". These describe what the requests contain and the order they use. They don't name a library, algorithm, signature, type or interface that must do the work.
- The cited `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` only supplies context for which prompt counts as the system prompt. It is cited, not refined.

The text names no library, type, signature or delegation, so evidence from tests covers it and no {impl} root is missing.

behavioral: The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`.

**Explicit checkpoints, Bedrock Claude.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs a two-request conversation, the second after a reasoning turn. For every request it asserts three things:
- The `system` array is the system text followed by one `cachePoint`.
- The last content block of the last message is a `cachePoint`.
- The body contains exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences.

This covers "every provider request", "after the system prompt", "end of its last message", and "one" checkpoint at each position.

**Checkpoints do not change content.** The same test runs a non-caching model (`fixture-uncached-model`) and asserts that the cached body, with `cachePoint` blocks stripped by `without_cache_points`, equals the plain body for each request. This also covers the "when the backend and model support caching" condition, because the non-caching model gets no `cachePoint`. The unit test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]` backs this up:
- `bedrock_caches` is true for Claude and Nova models and false for Llama and the fixture model.
- `place_cache_checkpoints` changes only the `cache` option, checked by comparing serialized requests.
- Checkpoints are still requested after a reasoning turn.

**OpenAI.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` checks each of the three OpenAI obligations:
- The `instructions` and `tools` fields are identical across the two requests.
- The second request's `input` begins with the first request's `input` unchanged, followed by the `function_call` and `function_call_output` in order.
- `assert_no_checkpoints` recursively rejects `cachePoint`, `cache_control`, and `cache_point` or `cache_checkpoint` block types in every request body.

The prompt-parts content is context only. The system prompt text is checked separately by `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and needs no test here.

I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the requirement.

definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
distributed requirement, non-distributed requirement, example, citation review, site
review. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
